optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Data Quality Engineer, Logistics Delivery Services

professionalSummary.text: Data Quality Engineer with 2.5 years of end-to-end ownership of scan-event data quality programmes for logistics delivery services, including rule enforcement decisions, rule-engine development, and cross-functional coordination.
professionalSummary.witness: Owned the scan-event data quality programme for the delivery division for two and a half years, deciding which quality rules were enforced at ingestion as the programme's named owner in the data governance register

experienceHighlights.text: Decided which quality rules were enforced at ingestion as the named owner in the data governance register, switching rules between warn and block modes under personal authority.
experienceHighlights.witness: deciding which quality rules were enforced at ingestion as the programme's named owner in the data governance register

experienceHighlights.text: Built and maintained the quality-rule engine (Python rules evaluated in the ingestion pipeline) and quality dashboards showing rule breaches per depot and driver app version.
experienceHighlights.witness: Built and maintained the quality-rule engine (Python rules evaluated in the ingestion pipeline) and the quality dashboards showing rule breaches per depot and driver app version.

experienceHighlights.text: Led weekly data quality reviews with depot operations, deciding which breaches were escalated to depot managers and recording decisions in the review log.
experienceHighlights.witness: Led the weekly data quality review with depot operations, deciding which breaches were escalated to depot managers and recording the decisions in the review log.

experienceHighlights.text: Coordinated rule changes with settlement and platform teams through the data change process, recording ownership boundaries: settlement team owned settlement calculation, platform team owned ingestion pipeline, candidate owned rules.
experienceHighlights.witness: Coordinated rule changes with the settlement and platform teams through the data change process, recording that the settlement team owned the settlement calculation and the platform team owned the ingestion pipeline while I owned the rules.

experienceHighlights.text: Documented rule definitions, limitations, and hand-over conditions for each rule release, with pipeline rule-release identifiers as verification.
experienceHighlights.witness: Work sample: the data governance register entry naming the candidate as programme owner, the rule change log showing mode switches under the candidate's user id and one weekly review log, with the pipeline's rule-release identifiers as a verification trail.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Data governance register entry naming candidate as programme owner, rule change log showing mode switches under candidate's user ID, and weekly review log with pipeline rule-release identifiers as verification trail.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the data governance register entry naming the candidate as programme owner, the rule change log showing mode switches under the candidate's user id and one weekly review log, with the pipeline's rule-release identifiers as a verification trail.

skills.text: Python (for rule-engine development), data governance, cross-functional coordination, data quality rule management, dashboard development.
skills.witness: Built and maintained the quality-rule engine (Python rules evaluated in the ingestion pipeline)

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish end-to-end ownership of scan-event data quality programme, rule-engine development, dashboards, weekly reviews, coordination with teams, and documentation of rule releases. They do not establish the candidate's specific technical skills beyond Python, nor the impact of data quality on settlement outcomes.

decisionBoundary.statement: All requirements are supported by evidence, but human review is required to assess the candidate's ability to lead data quality reviews and coordinate with teams.

role.roleTitle: Data Quality Engineer, Logistics Delivery Services

evidence.text: Owned the scan-event data quality programme for the delivery division for two and a half years, deciding which quality rules were enforced at ingestion as the programme's named owner in the data governance register, and switching rules between warn and block modes under my own authority.
evidence.notes: Named owner in data governance register

evidence.text: Built and maintained the quality-rule engine (Python rules evaluated in the ingestion pipeline) and the quality dashboards showing rule breaches per depot and driver app version.
Led the weekly data quality review with depot operations, deciding which breaches were escalated to depot managers and recording the decisions in the review log.

Coordinated rule changes with the settlement and platform teams through the data change process, recording that the settlement team owned the settlement calculation and the platform team owned the ingestion pipeline while I owned the rules.

Work sample: the data governance register entry naming the candidate as programme owner, the rule change log showing mode switches under the candidate's user id and one weekly review log, with the pipeline's rule-release identifiers as a verification trail.
evidence.notes: Rule definitions and hand-over conditions documented

supportedClaims.witness: deciding which quality rules were enforced at ingestion as the programme's named owner in the data governance register

supportedClaims.claim: Built and maintained the quality-rule engine (Python rules evaluated in the ingestion pipeline) and quality dashboards showing rule breaches per depot and driver app version.
supportedClaims.witness: Built and maintained the quality-rule engine (Python rules evaluated in the ingestion pipeline) and the quality dashboards showing rule breaches per depot and driver app version.

supportedClaims.claim: Led weekly data quality reviews with depot operations, deciding which breaches were escalated to depot managers and recording decisions in the review log.
supportedClaims.witness: Led the weekly data quality review with depot operations, deciding which breaches were escalated to depot managers and recording the decisions in the review log.

supportedClaims.claim: Coordinated rule changes with settlement and platform teams through the data change process, recording ownership boundaries: settlement team owned settlement calculation, platform team owned ingestion pipeline, candidate owned rules.
supportedClaims.witness: Coordinated rule changes with the settlement and platform teams through the data change process, recording that the settlement team owned the settlement calculation and the platform team owned the ingestion pipeline while I owned the rules.

supportedClaims.claim: Documented rule definitions, limitations, and hand-over conditions for each rule release, with pipeline rule-release identifiers as verification.
supportedClaims.witness: Work sample: the data governance register entry naming the candidate as programme owner, the rule change log showing mode switches under the candidate's user id and one weekly review log, with the pipeline's rule-release identifiers as a verification trail.

interviewSignalRisks.text: candidate can attend a rule-engine walkthrough next week; notice period is one month.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify availability and notice period during interview

followUpQuestions.question: Can you describe a specific instance where you had to switch a rule from warn to block mode, and what factors influenced that decision?
How did you ensure the quality-rule engine's Python rules were scalable and maintainable as the number of scan events increased?
What metrics did you use to measure the success of the weekly data quality reviews with depot operations?
How did you handle disagreements with the settlement team about rule changes that impacted settlement calculations?
Can you provide an example of a rule limitation you documented and how it affected the hand-over process?

humanReviewChecklist: Verify the candidate's ability to lead data quality reviews
Assess coordination skills with settlement and platform teams
Confirm technical depth in Python rule-engine development
hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: All requirements are supported by evidence from the candidate's CV, work samples, and reference call. The materials establish end-to-end ownership of the scan-event data quality programme, rule-engine development, dashboards, weekly reviews, coordination with teams, and documentation of rule releases. The only gap is the lack of evidence on the impact of data quality on settlement outcomes, which is not a requirement but may be relevant for the role.
limitations: The materials do not establish the candidate's specific technical skills beyond Python
The materials do not establish the impact of data quality on settlement outcomes
